t: Red-billed oxpeckers: vampires or tickbirds? | Behavioral Ecology ...
s: March 1, 2000 - Many recent studies have shown that classic examples of mutualism are either far more complicated than originally believed, or that they are not mutualisms at all. Red-billed oxpeckers (Buphagus erythrorhynchus) are just such an example of an “adaptive story.” These small birds feed almost exclusively on what they can glean from the skin of large African mammals.

t: Oxpecker | Types, Diet, & Facts | Britannica
s: July 20, 1998 - Oxpecker, either of two species of the African bird genus Buphagus. Both species are brown, measure about 20 cm (8 inches) long, and have wide bills, stiff tails, and sharp claws.

t: The Oxpecker: Nature's Feathered Caretaker
s: October 1, 2025 - Both species share olive-brown plumage, stiff tails used for balance, and strong claws that help them cling onto their mammal hosts. Measuring around 20cm (8 inches) in length, oxpeckers may seem small, but their behaviour is anything but timid.
